Demo · Why we built it
Lunar Landing Site Navigator
We compare candidate lunar landing sites using real NASA/JPL ephemeris and LRO LOLA terrain, against engineering criteria.
Principles we started with
Real data · JPL Horizons API and LRO LOLA, no invented values
Constraints · 10° landing slope limit, Sun 1–2° above the horizon, Earth link
Architecture · modular backend, dependency-free Python, single-page UI
Safety · local access only, no launch before the tests pass

backend/__init__.py · 0 bytes
Makes a package
Empty on purpose: it lets server.py write from backend.nasa import …
backend/nasa.py · 179 lines · JPL Horizons client
Targets only 10 Sun or 399 Earth, observed from the Moon: CENTER = coord@301
Observer = SITE_COORD longitude, latitude, LOLA height; AIRLESS: no refraction on the Moon
Validates inputs: 1–90 days, 1–24 h step, max 750 samples; a missing or repeated table row raises an error
backend/probe.py · 24 lines
One-command field check
py -3 -m backend.probe runs DEM source, topocentric state, Δv, propellant and Horizons in turn.

2
Code · analysis.py 1220 lines + ephemeris.py
Terrain, light and landing, computed from first principles
LOLA DEM grid with bilinear and bicubic interpolation
Horizon mask: 180 azimuths × 103 distances out to 150 km, 18 540 samples per site
The Sun is a disk, not a point: radius 0.266°
Local gravity with J2, slope and surface normal
Descent simulation, Tsiolkovsky propellant and visibility windows
ephemeris.py · fallback
Meeus + IAU 2009 Moon frame, within 0.005° of Horizons
Great-circle step · horizon ray
sin φ₂ = sin φ₁ cos σ + cos φ₁ sin σ cos α
Exact geometric elevation angle · θ = s / R
el = atan2( r₁ cos θ − r₀ , r₁ sin θ )
Visible fraction of the solar disk · h = el / 0.266°
f = 1 − ( acos h − h √(1 − h²) ) / π
Gravity with J2 · r = R + h(LOLA)
g = GM/r² · [ 1 − 1.5 J₂ (R/r)² (3 sin²φ − 1) ]
Tsiolkovsky propellant · Isp = 311 s
m(prop) = m₀ ( 1 − e^(−Δv / (Isp · g₀)) )

Elevation time series and horizon mask
Same Sun, two fates: why the Sun and Earth curves differ
Sun elevation · 24 h
Earth elevation · 24 h
Horizon mask · 360°
The Sun rises and sets
The Moon turns once in 29.5 days, so the Sun moves about 12° a day. At Apollo 17 it climbs −6.03° → +5.40°; at Shackleton it skims the horizon, 1.66°–1.80°.
The Earth barely moves
The Moon always shows Earth the same face; Earth only rocks a few degrees by libration. At A it stays near 54°; at B near −3.6°, it never rises.
Terrain cuts both
Sample log, A 15:00: Sun +1.12°, horizon 8.75° → shadow. B 00:00: Sun +1.66°, horizon 0.98° → lit. 0 h vs 15.33 h of terrain-clear sunlight.
